verses.1: For the music director, with stringed instruments. A psalm by David.
verses.2: When I called, you answered me, God of my righteousness. In distress you opened the way before me. Be gracious to me and hear my prayer.
verses.3: Mortal men, how long will your hearts be weighed down? Why do you love emptiness and seek lies? Selah.
verses.4: Know this: the LORD has set apart the righteous one for himself. The LORD hears when I call to him.
verses.5: Be angry, but do not sin. Meditate within your hearts on your beds and be silent. Selah.
verses.6: Offer sacrifices of righteousness and trust in the LORD.
verses.7: Many are saying, “Who can show us good?” May the light of your face, LORD, shine on us.
verses.8: You have given joy to my heart, greater than in the time of their grain and wine, when they were multiplied.
verses.9: In peace I will lie down and sleep, for you alone, LORD, give me a place of safety.

notes:
Notes
- v. 2: "In distress you opened the way before me" — the Hebrew reads "in the tight place you opened for me," and "tight place" is a common metaphor for distress.
- v. 3: "your hearts be weighed down" — the Hebrew literally says "your hearts are heavy," but the translation renders it as a rhetorical question.
- v. 8: "in the time of their grain and wine" — the Hebrew uses "when their grain was full and their wine was abundant," but the meaning is rendered in a natural way.
